https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-new.text: Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested by federal authorities in Miami on Saturday. The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests.The charges announced by British prosecutors significantly expand the case against the social media influencers, who have consistently denied all allegations.Officials said the warrant remains sealed. The precise legal basis filed in the United States has not yet been made public. A person familiar with the matter told The Guardian that the arrests were made following a UK extradition request.Also read: Why Andrew and his brother Tristan Tate were arrested in Miami? What we know so far New charges against Andrew, Tristan TateThe UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) announced fresh charges against both brothers after receiving additional evidence from Bedfordshire Police.Andrew Tate, 39, now faces seven further rape charges, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm, and 19 additional offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Prosecutors said the alleged offences occurred between July 2010 and August 2017.Tristan Tate, 38, faces one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation stemming from the same investigation. The CPS said the latest evidence increases the total number of alleged victims in the case to seven.The brothers already face a separate UK criminal case. Andrew Tate has been charged with 10 offences, including rape, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain involving three alleged victims. Tristan Tate faces 11 charges connected to one alleged victim. Both men have denied all wrongdoing.Also read: Fact check: Is Gov. Andy Beshear trying to fill Mitch McConnel Senate seat as he remains absent?Will the Tate brothers be extradited to the UK?The arrests do not automatically mean Andrew and Tristan Tate will be transferred to Britain.Under US law, a federal court must first determine whether the UK extradition request satisfies the requirements of the US-UK Extradition Treaty. The brothers will have the opportunity to challenge the request through the American court system. If the court certifies the extradition, the final decision generally rests with the US Secretary of State.The UK proceedings are also separate from the brothers' criminal case in Romania. Romanian prosecutors charged both men after their 2022 arrests with human trafficking, rape and forming an organized criminal group.Earlier this year, a UK High Court judge rejected the brothers' attempt to obtain the identities of the women accusing them in one of the British cases.

https://www.planetf1.com/news/aston-mart.text: Aston Martin team owner Lawrence Stroll observed the B-spec AMR26 in action in Hungary Martin Brundle caught up with Aston Martin team owner Lawrence Stroll ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix, where the B-spec AMR26 hit the track. It is good news for the folks at Aston Martin , as Stroll declared himself “very satisfied” with the step. The upgraded Honda engine is coming next, while team boss Adrian Newey teased more to come. Aston Martin ‘very big step’ declared by Lawrence Stroll Want more PlanetF1.com coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust. After early F1 2026 pain for Aston Martin and Honda, hope arrived at the Hungarian Grand Prix as a 16-part upgrade for the AMR26 arrived. The results were positive. From comfortably last over recent rounds, Aston Martin got a car into Q2 courtesy of Fernando Alonso. During the Hungarian Grand Prix, Aston Martin went wheel-to-wheel with Williams, Alpine, and Haas as Lance Stroll finished 13th and Alonso 14th. That has helped lift the mood within the Aston Martin camp, especially as as the correlation between virtual and real world aligned for the upgraded AMR26. That correlation is important as it suggests that, going forward, Aston Martin can have confidence that future developments will yield the expected anticipated performance; not only for F1 2026 but into next year, too. The team has maintained a cautious outward approach despite positive early signs from the upgrades. Team owner Lawrence Stroll did though give a glowing review when speaking with Sky F1’s Martin Brundle ahead of lights out in Hungary. Conducting his iconic ‘grid walk’ segment, Brundle spotted and approached Stroll, who rarely gives interviews. “Lawrence, your car is going a bit better. Are you satisfied with the improvement with your car this weekend?” Brundle asked. Stroll confirmed: “Yeah, obviously we’ve made a very big step forward. One of many to come. So yes, very satisfied. “Thanks to all the hard work from all the boys and the girls at the factory to make it happen.” Stroll concluded that it was a “good start” to the recovery process for his team. The proposal was submitted by the Minister of Justice and National Integration in accordance with the provisions of the Extradition Act, No. 5 of 1995. The Act provides for foreign nationals convicted in Sri Lanka to serve their sentences in their home countries. It also allows Sri Lankan nationals convicted and sentenced to imprisonment in another country to be extradited to Sri Lanka to serve the remaining portion of their sentences. The proposed agreement with Poland is intended to establish a framework for such extradition arrangements between the two countries. Beállítom The investigating judge has approved the motion filed by the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office and has on Tuesday ordered that a European and international arrest warrant be issued for Ádám Matolcsy and György Stofa. Ádám Matolcsy’s father, György Matolcsy served as governor of the Hungarian National Bank between 2013-2026 . Matolcsy was detained last week on suspicion of having committed economic fraud and other crimes resulting in particularly significant financial loss, related to a minor thread of the investigation into what has become known in Hungary as the MNB-case. During his father’s tenure as head of the central bank, Ádám Matolcsy and his closest friends amassed huge fortunes-in part through winning overpriced, state-funded tenders of the institution. As the former head of one of the bank’s companies (Optima Befektetési Zrt) established during this time, György Stofa played an important role in the maneuver attempted shortly before György Matolcsy's term at the central bank was up, but he had previously also appeared in the management of numerous companies linked to the central bank and played an active role in the story of Villa Nicole on Mykonos, which is linked to Ádám Matolcsy . According to a statement from the Budapest Metropolitan Court, neither Matolcsy Jr nor Stofa are currently residing at their registered Hungarian addresses. “At the same time, there is evidence that they have left the country and are presumably somewhere outside Europe. Nevertheless, the court found it justified to also search for them within the territory of the European Union,” the court wrote. The statement added that the details of the arrest warrants will become available in the registration systems once the administrative procedures are completed. The ruling will be sent to the Ministry of Justice and the National Center for International Criminal Cooperation (NEBEK), where the warrants will also be entered into the relevant international databases, namely those of Interpol and Europol. Thus, if the wanted person is stopped by police in, say Dubai or Vienna, the system will immediately indicate that there is an arrest warrant in effect against them. However, extradition is not automatic in this case either. Double criminality must first be verified. “In other words, the act which the wanted person is suspected of must be classified as a criminal offense in both the issuing country and the executing state,” Gergő Bozó, spokesperson for the Budapest Metropolitan Court, previously told Telex. Although there is a common misconception that if someone flees to a country with which Hungary has no bilateral extradition treaty (such as Thailand, the United Arab Emirates/Dubai, or certain Caribbean or South American states), they are beyond the reach of the law there, in reality, international criminal cooperation is much more complex. Even without an extradition treaty, Hungary may, within the framework of international legal assistance, request the offender’s extradition through diplomatic channels based on the so-called principle of reciprocity. If the receiving country agrees to extradite the wanted person—for example, based on the promise that Hungary will do the same in a similar future case—the extradition can take place. The order was issued by the same judge who, last Friday, ordered the arrest of György Matolcsy, the former governor of the Hungarian National Bank, Tamás Sándor, the permanent attorney for Ádám Matolcsy’s companies, and Mihály Valkó, a senior executive at a company linked to Ádám Matolcsy and his friend István Száraz. According to a statement from the Budapest Metropolitan Court, Ádám Matolcsy may be charged with acting as an instigator of economic fraud, causing particularly significant financial loss, as well as with instigating the use of a forged private document. György Stofa may have been an accomplice in economic fraud causing particularly significant financial loss, as well as in using a forged private document. As mentioned above, the former governor of the central bank and his associates are suspected of economic fraud resulting in particularly significant financial damage and other criminal offenses. Previously, on September 21, investigating prosecutors visited several locations in connection with one of the threads of the MNB case, including György Matolcsy’s home. According to the investigation, in the final days of Matolcsy being at the helm of the institution, and just a few days prior to the State Audit Office publishing its report about the MNB case and the fate of the 650 million euros worth of forints, there was some unusual restructuring around PADME, the central bank's foundation. Specifically, on February 28, 2025, right before Matolcsy’s departure, Optima Investment Ltd., which managed the foundation’s assets, transferred the shares of Optima Investment Fund Management to a private equity fund called Közép-Európai III. Magántőkealap under a contract described as a securities loan. Behind the complicated company names stood a familiar figure: the private equity fund was managed by Quartz Investment Fund Management, whose majority owner was István Száraz-a longtime friend of Ádám Matolcsy, the governor’s son. Under this arrangement, it was not the foundation’s assets themselves that were sold. Instead, the ownership rights of the company which played a key role in managing those assets would have been transferred to the private equity fund for several years. However, the plan was thwarted by the arrival of Mihály Varga: after the new governor of the central bank took office, the foundation’s former board of trustees stepped down, and the controversial contract was terminated within a few days. Varga and his team were not satisfied with simply reversing the transaction though: they launched an investigation and, in April, filed a criminal complaint. Quartz later tried to explain the transaction by claiming that it intended to provide professional assistance to Optima; however, documents obtained by Telex suggested that the ownership restructuring was likely prepared well in advance. Although Ádám Matolcsy did not officially feature in this story—and there had previously been no evidence that he was even informally involved in the matter—those familiar with the case say that Stofa is his trusted associate. As for Ádám Matolcsy’s role, the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office said that the true purpose of the sham securities loan agreement was to “transfer the right to control the assets of the PADME Foundation to a group of individuals over whom György Matolcsy would retain influence even after his term as central bank governor expired, thereby enabling him and his son to make investments in line with their own interests for the purpose of financial gain.” However, this move resulted in a financial loss of several hundred million forints.
